questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Ozone in stratosphere is depleted by
questions.solution:
The depletion of the ozone layer in the stratosphere is primarily caused by chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs).

CFCs are compounds containing chlorine, fluorine, and carbon. When these compounds reach the stratosphere, they are decomposed by ultraviolet radiation to release chlorine free radicals ($\mathrm{Cl}^{\bullet}$).

The chlorine radical acts as a catalyst in the destruction of ozone ($\mathrm{O}_3$) through the following reactions:

$\mathrm{Cl}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O}_3 \rightarrow \mathrm{ClO}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O}_2\mathrm{ClO}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O} \rightarrow \mathrm{Cl}^{\bullet} + \mathrm{O}_2$

Among the given options, $\mathrm{CF}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$ (dichlorodifluoromethane, commonly known as Freon-12) is a well-known CFC responsible for this ozone depletion process.

Answer: $\mathrm{CF}_2\mathrm{Cl}_2$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following gas is responsible for acid rain?
questions.solution:
Acid rain is primarily caused by the emission of sulphur dioxide ($SO_2$) and nitrogen oxides ($NO_x$).

These gases react with water vapor and other chemicals in the atmosphere to form sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) and nitric acid ($HNO_3$), which then fall to the ground as acid rain.

Among the given options, sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide are the primary pollutants responsible for this phenomenon.

Answer: Sulphur dioxide and nitrogen oxide

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Carbon monoxide is poisonous to human beings because
options: it binds 300 times more strongly to haemoglobin than oxygen.
it leads to coagulation of blood.
questions.solution:
Carbon monoxide ($CO$) has a very high affinity for haemoglobin, which is approximately 300 times greater than that of oxygen ($O_{2}$).

When $CO$ is inhaled, it binds to the iron atom in the haemoglobin molecule to form carboxyhaemoglobin, which is much more stable than oxyhaemoglobin.

This binding prevents haemoglobin from transporting oxygen to the tissues, leading to oxygen deprivation and toxicity.

Answer: it binds 300 times more strongly to haemoglobin than oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following particulate matter is emitted from vehicles?
questions.solution:
Particulate matter refers to solid or liquid particles suspended in the air. Among the given options, Lead (Pb) is a well-known heavy metal pollutant emitted from vehicle exhausts, particularly in regions where leaded gasoline was historically used or due to the wear and tear of vehicle components containing lead. Carbon monoxide (CO) is a gaseous pollutant, not particulate matter. Tin (Sn) and Selenium (Se) are not primary particulate emissions associated with standard vehicle exhaust systems.

Answer: Pb

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.q: Which of the following compounds is responsible for depletion of ozone layer?
questions.solution:
Freons are chlorofluorocarbons introduced into the atmosphere from aerosol sprays and refrigerating equipments. They have a very long life time and when they reach stratosphere, they undergo photochemical decomposition and destroy ozone by the following sequence of reactions.
$\mathrm{CF}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}_{2} \stackrel{h v}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CF}_{2} \mathrm{Cl}^{\circ}+\mathrm{Cl}^{\circ}\mathrm{CFCl}_{3} \stackrel{h v}{\longrightarrow} \mathrm{CFCl}_{2}^{\circ}+\mathrm{Cl}^{\circ}\mathrm{Cl}^{\circ}+\mathrm{O}_{3} \longrightarrow \mathrm{ClO}^{\circ}+\mathrm{O}_{2}\mathrm{ClO}^{\circ}+[\mathrm{O}] \longrightarrow \mathrm{Cl}^{\circ}+\mathrm{O}_{2}$
